_source: English Appendix 1: Spelling (DfE 2013), Year 1 and Year 2 common exception words. Open Government Licence v3.0. Meanings written for Wordbright (simple, for ages 5-8). Not playable on the board and so left out: a, I (one letter), Mr, Mrs, Christmas (capital letters).

year_1.the: A word used before a thing we know about, as in 'the cat'.
year_1.of: Belonging to or part of something.
year_1.are: A form of 'be', as in 'we are'.
year_1.were: A form of 'be' in the past, as in 'they were'.
year_1.was: A form of 'be' in the past, as in 'it was'.
year_1.is: A form of 'be', as in 'she is'.
year_1.you: The person someone is talking to.
year_1.he: A boy or man already talked about.
year_1.she: A girl or woman already talked about.
year_1.we: The speaker and other people together.
year_1.go: To move from one place to another.
year_1.by: Next to, or done by someone.
year_1.love: A very strong, warm feeling for someone.
year_1.come: To move towards someone or a place.
year_1.some: A few, or an amount of.
year_1.friend: Someone you like and who likes you.
year_1.push: To press something away from you.
year_1.full: Holding as much as it can.

year_2.door: What you open to go into a room or building.
year_2.floor: The part of a room you walk on.
year_2.mind: The part of you that thinks.
year_2.wild: Living in nature, not looked after by people.
year_2.climb: To go up using hands and feet.
year_2.old: Having lived or been around a long time.
year_2.hold: To keep something in your hands.
year_2.even: Flat and smooth, or a number like 2, 4 or 6.
year_2.beautiful: Very lovely to look at or hear.
year_2.class: A group of pupils who learn together.
year_2.grass: Green plants that cover fields and lawns.
year_2.pass: To go by, or to hand something to someone.
year_2.plant: A living thing that grows in soil.
year_2.bath: A big tub you wash in.
year_2.move: To go from one place to another.
year_2.prove: To show that something is true.
year_2.sugar: A sweet food used in cakes and drinks.
year_2.eye: The part of the body you see with.
year_2.would: A word for what might happen.
year_2.any: One or some, no matter which.
year_2.money: Coins and notes used to buy things.
year_2.parents: A mum and dad, or the people who look after a child.
